def amend_extraction(extraction_id: int, field: str, value: str, reason: str,
                     session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Change a field of `_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS` on an EXISTING row -- and ONLY those.

    Every other refusal here mirrors the one `insert_extraction` runs at write
    time, because grading a pre-existing row after the fact must not be able to
    reach a state add-extraction itself refuses to create.
    """
    if field not in _AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS:
        raise Refusal(
            f"amend-extraction: --field {field!r} refused. Only "
            f"{sorted(_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS)} may be amended here -- a wrong "
            f"claimed_value or claim_text is a SECOND ROW and a contest (D-0168), "
            f"not an overwrite. Write another `db.py add-extraction` if the "
            f"disagreement is over the value or the claim itself.")
    reason = (reason or "").strip()
    if not reason:
        raise Refusal(
            "amend-extraction: --reason is required. An amendment that cannot say "
            "why cannot be contested.")
    value = (value or "").strip()
    if not value:
        raise Refusal("amend-extraction: --value is required and must not be blank.")
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        # SELECT * rather than a hand-listed column set. The list here was
        # "extraction_id, ref_id, figure_role, comparator, claim_type, notes" and
        # broke with IndexError the moment _AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS grew -- a second
        # place naming the amendable columns, one line below the constant that
        # names them. Two lists, one truth.
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?",
            (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"amend-extraction: extraction_id {extraction_id}: no "
                          f"such row.")
        # BOTH GATES, DERIVED, ON EVERY AMENDABLE FIELD. The first version of this gated
        # one column by name -- `if field == "root_ref_id"` -- twenty lines below a
        # generic check_declared in amend_source, which is the field-by-field shape rule 8
        # forbids and which this very commit had just criticised. fk_declared reads
        # PRAGMA foreign_key_list, so it is a no-op where no FK is declared and covers
        # every amendable reference the day one becomes amendable.
        dbcore.fk_declared(conn, "source_value_extractions", field, value,
                           f"amend-extraction --field {field}")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "source_value_extractions", field, value,
                              "amend-extraction")
        if field == "jurisdiction":
            # No CHECK or FK on the column; the declared vocabulary is base_jurisdictions (I7),
            # checked exactly as amend-source --field jurisdiction checks it.
            dbcore.check_jurisdiction(value, "amend-extraction --field jurisdiction")

        old = row[field]
        if field == "value_as_written":
            # The shared number rule, against the row's own quote and figure: a stored row is
            # brought into line without touching either. (The quote was verified when written.)
            _require_stated_numbers(row["claim_text"] or "", row["claimed_value"], row["claim_type"],
                                    value, "--claim-text", "amend-extraction")
        if field == "extraction_status" and value == "verified":
            _require_full_scan_for_verified(conn, row["ref_id"], row["parameter_id"],
                                            "amend-extraction")
        if field == "figure_role":
            if row["claim_type"] == "absent" and value != "finding":
                raise Refusal(
                    f"amend-extraction: extraction {extraction_id} has "
                    f"claim_type='absent' -- absence IS a finding, so figure_role "
                    f"must stay 'finding', not {value!r}.")
            if value == "derived":
                base_edge = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM extraction_relations WHERE from_extraction_id=? "
                    "AND relation='derived_from' AND input_role='base'",
                    (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
                if not base_edge:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"amend-extraction: figure_role='derived' requires at "
                        f"least one derived_from edge carrying input_role=base. "
                        f"extraction {extraction_id} has none -- add one with "
                        f"relate-extraction first.")
            if _why := dbcore.comparator_refusal(value, row["claim_type"], row["comparator"]):
                raise Refusal(f"amend-extraction: extraction {extraction_id}: {_why}. Set it first with "
                              f"amend-extraction --field comparator. Nothing was written.")
            if value == "claim":
                bad = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT relation FROM extraction_relations "
                    "WHERE from_extraction_id=? AND relation IN "
                    "('insufficient','audited_against') LIMIT 1",
                    (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
                if bad:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"amend-extraction: extraction {extraction_id} carries a "
                        f"{bad[0]!r} edge -- a row finding the baseline inadequate "
                        f"or audited against it asserts no absolute value, so "
                        f"figure_role cannot be 'claim'. Leave it 'finding'.")

        if old == value:
            # THE REASON IS STILL RECORDED. This path used to return early and DISCARD
            # --reason, although the flag's own help says it is "Appended to notes, never
            # overwriting it". A session that re-examined a row, found the value already
            # right, and wrote down what it had learned got a silent no-op -- the finding
            # vanished. Measured on this batch: a correction recording that a quote had
            # been confirmed against a rendered page image, and that the row's page
            # locator means the one-based PDF page rather than the index an earlier note
            # called it, was written and lost.
            #
            # "I checked, and it was already correct, and here is what I found" is a real
            # result and often a more useful one than a change, because it is the only
            # trace that the checking happened at all.
            stamp = dbcore.now()
            marker = f" || {stamp[:10]} {field} CONFIRMED {value} ({reason})"
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE source_value_extractions SET notes=?, updated_at=?, "
                "updated_by_session=? WHERE extraction_id=?",
                ((row["notes"] or "").rstrip() + marker, stamp, session, extraction_id))
            return {"extraction_id": extraction_id, "field": field, "changed": False,
                    "reason": "already this value; the reason is recorded on notes",
                    "dry_run": dry_run}

        # A CHANGE of a column the engine reads (figure_role, comparator, extraction_method here)
        # decides what a row supplies (a value, direction, a confirmation) and what bound it
        # composes, so the marker and the interval; a live determination was written on the
        # grading it had. Recording that a value was checked and is already right (above) changes nothing,
        # and a row of a superseded source is never gathered, so neither is refused.
        if field in dbcore.ENGINE_EXTRACTION_COLUMNS and conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=? AND superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL",
                (row["ref_id"],)).fetchone():
            live = dbcore.live_determinations_linked(conn, extraction_id)
            if live:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"amend-extraction: extraction {extraction_id} is in the provenance of live "
                    f"determination(s) {', '.join(map(str, live))}; amending {field} would "
                    f"change what that answer rests on without re-deciding it. Retire the "
                    f"specification first (db.py retire-specification), amend, then "
                    f"re-determine. Nothing was written.")

        stamp = dbcore.now()
        old_disp = "NULL" if old is None else old
        marker = f" || {stamp[:10]} {field} SET {old_disp} -> {value} ({reason})"
        merged = (row["notes"] or "").rstrip() + marker
        conn.execute(
            f"UPDATE source_value_extractions SET {field}=?, notes=?, "
            f"updated_at=?, updated_by_session=? WHERE extraction_id=?",
            (value, merged, stamp, session, extraction_id))
        if field == "figure_role" and value == "derived":
            # Checked on the UPDATED row, so the view sees it: a base edge alone is accepted above (the delta
            # may come next), and relate-extraction runs this same check when the delta edge arrives.
            _refuse_derived_mismatch(conn, extraction_id, "amend-extraction")
    return {"extraction_id": extraction_id, "field": field, "old": old, "new": value,
            "changed": True, "dry_run": dry_run}

===== v_root_id_conflicts
CREATE VIEW v_root_id_conflicts AS
    SELECT 'ref_id_has_multiple_root_ids' AS conflict_type,
           root_ref_id AS conflict_key,
           COUNT(DISTINCT root_id) AS distinct_count
    FROM source_value_extractions
    WHERE root_ref_id IS NOT NULL AND root_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY root_ref_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT root_id) > 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'root_id_spans_multiple_ref_ids' AS conflict_type,
           root_id AS conflict_key,
           COUNT(DISTINCT root_ref_id) AS distinct_count
    FROM source_value_extractions
    WHERE root_ref_id IS NOT NULL AND root_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY root_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT root_ref_id) > 1
===== v_value_independence
CREATE VIEW v_value_independence AS
    SELECT sve.parameter_id,
           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
           COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(sve.root_ref_id, sve.root_id)) AS independent_root_count
    FROM source_value_extractions sve
    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
    WHERE sve.root_type IN ('measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                            'derived_calculation')
      AND (sve.root_ref_id IS NOT NULL
           OR sve.root_id IN (SELECT root_id FROM external_root_registry))
      -- 104: active parameters only; a retired parameter's extractions are history.
      AND p.status = 'active'
    GROUP BY sve.parameter_id, t.canonical_en
===== v_unregistered_roots
CREATE VIEW v_unregistered_roots AS
    SELECT sve.extraction_id,
           sve.slug,
           sve.parameter_id,
           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
           sve.root_id,
           'unregistered' AS defect
    FROM source_value_extractions sve
    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
                           AND p.status = 'active'
    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
    WHERE sve.root_id IS NOT NULL
      AND sve.root_ref_id IS NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM external_root_registry err
          WHERE err.root_id = sve.root_id)

    UNION ALL

    SELECT sve.extraction_id,
           sve.slug,
           sve.parameter_id,
           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
           sve.root_id,
           'rootless' AS defect
    FROM source_value_extractions sve
    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
                           AND p.status = 'active'
    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
    WHERE sve.root_id IS NULL
      AND sve.root_ref_id IS NULL
      AND sve.root_type IS NOT NULL
      AND sve.root_type NOT IN ('untraced', 'derived_calculation')
===== v_registry_duplicate_descriptions
CREATE VIEW v_registry_duplicate_descriptions AS
    SELECT LOWER(TRIM(description)) AS normalised_description,
           COUNT(*) AS stub_count,
           GROUP_CONCAT(root_id, ', ') AS root_ids
    FROM external_root_registry
    GROUP BY LOWER(TRIM(description))
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

      names neither the source nor the fix. An extraction is a reading OF a source;
      one that names no admitted source is a claim about nothing.

    * A `root_id` the registry does not hold (`external_root_registry`; migration 114).

      NOT NULL column carrying the source's own words; `claim_text`,
      `source_section` and all 16 `loc_*` columns are nullable, so without this the
      happy path writes a row with ZERO verbatim from the source it read. The
      guarantee is the CLI's, not the schema's — say so rather than implying the
      table enforces it.

content.content:
## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

`MOVE` (movement disorders) and `VES` (vestibular disorders) sit in the identity registry as populations, though the owner has agreed they are access needs, and the needs that carry them already exist (`A-PRECISION` absorbs movement disorders, `A-STABLE` vestibular disorders). Nothing can retire an identity code and say where its readers should go instead, so a writer given `MOVE` still accepts it as an identity.

**Evidence command** (read-only):

```
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([r[1] for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(base_taxonomy_identity)')]);print(c.execute(\"select identity_code,status,description from base_taxonomy_identity where identity_code in ('MOVE','VES')\").fetchall());print(c.execute(\"select need_code,absorbs from access_needs where need_code in ('A-PRECISION','A-STABLE')\").fetchall())"
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);T=[t for (t,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")];print({t+'.'+r[1]:c.execute('select count(*) from \"'+t+'\" where \"'+r[1]+'\" in (?,?)',('MOVE','VES')).fetchone()[0] for t in T for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(\"'+t+'\")') if r[1] in ('identity_code','target_population','pop_a','pop_b','parent_code')})"
```

**Expected output today:** no column for a successor need; both codes `active`; both needs present; every identity-bearing column holds 0 rows of either code (only the registry rows name them). If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. Schema migration: `base_taxonomy_identity.superseded_by_need TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code)`, with a CHECK that it is set only when `status = 'deprecated'`. Create, copy, drop, rename; recreate every view and index that names the table (`select type, name from sqlite_master where sql like '%base_taxonomy_identity%'`). Never type the migration number: derive it (`ls scripts/migrations | grep -E '^[0-9]{3}_' | sort | tail -1`, plus one), and end it by setting `PRAGMA user_version` to it. Run `python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py` before and after; apply only with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`; prove with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"` and `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep`.
1a. **[Added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] The identity successor, in the same migration.** Also add `base_taxonomy_identity.superseded_by_identity TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)`, and make the CHECK: a deprecated row has **exactly one** successor column set, an active row none (T-056 later adds a third successor column and widens this CHECK; it does not add a second mechanism). One mechanism serves both cases the owner's answers need: `SCI` retires to `WHEEL` (T-102) and `LMB` retires to `UPL` (T-116). A rename of the code was rejected: `identity_code` is a key other rows point at, and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires identifiers in place.
1b. **[Added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] Crossing-map rows retire in place.** `identity_icf_map` gains `retired_at`, `retired_by_session` and `retired_reason` (all NULL on a live row; a CHECK that the three are set together), and one verb `retire-population-icf-link --link-id N --reason "..." --session S`. Without it the refusal of item 2 is a dead end: `SCI` and `LMB` carry crossing rows (`select identity_code, count(*) from identity_icf_map where identity_code in ('SCI','LMB') group by 1`), and no verb removes or retires one. A crossing moves to a successor as a new row through the existing `add-population-icf-link` (its provenance names the old `link_id`) followed by retiring the old row; the table's `UNIQUE (identity_code, icf_code, mechanism)` already refuses a duplicate on the successor. A retired crossing is never un-retired. Every reader of `identity_icf_map` filters `retired_at IS NULL` first (the 2026-09-16 ruling's execution condition): find them with `git grep -n identity_icf_map -- scripts skills ':!scripts/migrations'` and `select name from sqlite_master where sql like '%identity_icf_map%'`.
2. One verb, `retire-identity --code (--need N | --to-identity C) --approval-ref H --reason R`, where `H` is the full text of a dated `## ` heading of `references/project-standards.md` found exactly once (corrected 2026-11-13 from a quoted ledger pointer: the one approval-pointer shape that T-024's `add-jurisdiction` and T-025's identity and pair verbs take for base admissions; T-025 section 4 names the check, `dbcore.require_approval_heading`; T-054 has no dependency on T-025, so it checks inline with `dbcore.ledger_heading_count`, as `add-jurisdiction` does today, and T-025's sweep converts that inline check to the helper when it merges. Chosen 2026-11-13, to avoid serialising T-054, T-056, T-114 and T-115 behind T-025), checked and printed in the result, not stored: sets `status = 'deprecated'` and `superseded_by_need`; never deletes. It refuses a code that any live row still carries (every column that takes an identity code, derived from the foreign keys into `base_taxonomy_identity`, not listed), naming the count and T-114's re-tag as the next action; and refuses a need that does not exist.
3. Every writer that takes an identity code refuses a `deprecated` one, and its message names the successor to use instead (read from whichever successor column is set). **Live rows** for the refusal of item 2 are rows with no retirement mark where the table has one (`identity_icf_map.retired_at`, and after T-018 `extraction_lens_links.retired_at`); `--to-identity` refuses a successor that is deprecated, is the code itself, or does not exist. `evidence_population_match.target_population` takes identity codes but has no foreign key, so the derivation by foreign keys misses it: name it explicitly in the refusal's message as a table to re-grade by judgment (never fan out a grade) and make `add-population-match` refuse a deprecated target like the other writers. Readers of `superseded_by_identity`: these refusal messages, and T-102 and T-116, which call the verb. Find the writers by the foreign keys and by the existing "LIVE code, not a retired one" help strings in `scripts/db.py`; locate by symbol.
python3 -c "import yaml,sys;print([c['id'] for c in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if sys.argv[1] in str(c)])" "$N"   # the check registry
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'   # prose and hand-written needles
```
If this task adds, renames or removes a verb, a table, a view or the text of a refusal, also run `python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --check` (it writes nothing) before your change and after it, and report the difference. It is red on the base: its failure count there is the base state, not yours; only a count above your before-run is yours. An object that returns 0 rows is unproven, not clean.

**Hits when this file was written:** not recorded (this file was written in the last fold pass of 2026-11-12, without running the sweep). Run the two `git grep` lines above with `-l` before you change anything; every file they print is a hit to judge as a caller or a mention.
-- 135_identity_successor.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- an identity code can be retired in place to the access need or the identity code that carries
-- it, and a crossing-map row can be retired in place. Tooling (workplan T-054, OD-37, OI-13 fold); no research rows.
--
-- WHY. MOVE and VES sit in the identity registry as populations, though the owner agreed they are access needs (OD-37),
-- and SCI and LMB are to be carried by WHEEL and UPL (T-102, T-116). Nothing could retire an identity code and say where
-- its readers should go, and nothing could retire a crossing row of identity_icf_map, so a retirement had no way to
-- finish. Identifiers are retired in place, never renamed or deleted (the 2026-09-16 ruling).
--
-- WHAT. base_taxonomy_identity gains superseded_by_need (an access_needs code) and superseded_by_identity (an identity
-- code). A DEPRECATED row names exactly ONE successor, an ACTIVE row none: one CHECK, carried by the second added
-- column (SQLite adds a column in place; a column CHECK may name the table's other columns, and it is tested on every
-- write of the row). identity_icf_map gains retired_at / retired_by_session / retired_reason, set together or not at all.
-- Every row stays; nothing is rewritten.
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_identity ADD COLUMN superseded_by_need TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code);
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_identity ADD COLUMN superseded_by_identity TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)
    CHECK ((status = 'deprecated' AND (superseded_by_need IS NOT NULL) + (superseded_by_identity IS NOT NULL) = 1)
        OR (status <> 'deprecated' AND superseded_by_need IS NULL AND superseded_by_identity IS NULL));

ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map ADD COLUMN retired_reason TEXT
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL AND retired_by_session IS NULL AND retired_reason IS NULL)
        OR (retired_at IS NOT NULL AND retired_by_session IS NOT NULL AND retired_reason IS NOT NULL));

# Adversarial pass: T-027, T-034, T-048, T-054

Read-only on `data/guidebook.db` throughout; its sha256 was unchanged at the end. All writers ran on copies in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/a9452ae4-7ff6-5ee7-9d22-5a8cc7e0001d/scratchpad/` with `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` set inline.

One thing moved under me: commit `f6dad812` (T-055, migration 136) landed mid-pass, so the working tree is now at schema 136, not 135. The T-054 before/after comparison used the blobs at `eca7ea8f^` and `eca7ea8f`; the rebuild comparison ran at 136.

Line numbers are from the working tree at `f6dad812`. Findings are ranked worst first.

---

## 1. T-054 — `add-medical --identity` writes a new crossing against a deprecated code (HIGH)

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py:7273` (the pre-check inside the add-medical writer).
- **Claim:** the commit message says `check_identity_live` refuses a deprecated code "in fk_declared (so every writer that uses it), add-population-icf-link, raise-determination-gate, add-population-match and the lens-link check". Task item 3 says every writer that takes an identity code refuses a deprecated one.
- **Failure:** add-medical checks existence with a raw `SELECT 1 FROM base_taxonomy_identity WHERE identity_code = ?`. It calls neither `fk_declared` nor `check_identity_live`.
- **Shown:** on a scratch copy, after `retire-identity --code MOVE --need A-PRECISION`:
  `db.py add-medical --code MD-ZZTEST --display-name Zed --description TASK-FIXTURE --icd11 8A00 --identity MOVE --relationship names --session ...` returned rc=0, and `identity_medical_map` then held `('MOVE','MD-ZZTEST','names',…)`.
- **Why the test missed it:** T054-04 exercises two verbs and one direct `dbcore.fk_declared` call. The writer list was never derived from the argparse surface.

## 2. T-034 — the research stage reads 7 of 203 searches (HIGH)

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py`, `cell_status`, `sfilter = "se.parameter_id = ?"`.
- **Claim:** `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md` says a mid-pipeline run reads it "so work already done is not repeated".
- **Failure:** `search_executions.parameter_id` is NULL on 196 of 203 rows; searches are keyed on `slug`.
- **Shown:** for parameter 3, cell-status returns research `held: []`, `examined_empty: []` and `scope_unrecorded` with 70 pairs. Yet 101 of its 122 figures carry the slug `accessible-circulation-geometry`, which has 168 logged searches, 50 of them admitting. The same output lists 57 evidence refs held — sources from searches it says do not exist.
  - `select parameter_id is null, count(*) from search_executions group by 1`
  - `select count(*), sum(coalesce(results_admitted,0)>0) from search_executions where slug in (select distinct slug from source_value_extractions where parameter_id=3)`
- **The gate examined nothing:**
  - T034-01's "independent" expectation uses the same `parameter_id` keying, on a parameter with zero searches, so it cannot go red on this.
  - The searched-pair subtraction has no live subject: `select count(*) from search_executions se join lang_jur_map m on m.language=upper(se.language) and m.jurisdiction=se.jurisdiction where se.parameter_id is not null` returns 0. It behaves correctly only on rows I seeded.

## 3. T-054 — carriers no verb can clear; the refusal's own remedy does not work (HIGH)

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py`, `_identity_carriers` and `retire_identity`.
- **Claim:** task 1b says that without a way out "the refusal of item 2 is a dead end", and names `SCI` retiring to `WHEEL`.
- **Failure:** `evidence_population_match` has no retirement mark, and the only statement in `db.py` that touches an existing row is `UPDATE evidence_population_match SET match_grade=` (`db.py:5971`).
- **Shown:** on scratch I retired all nine SCI crossing rows, then ran `amend-population-match --match-id session_2026-10-30-ramp--REF-01033-SCI --match-grade MISMATCH` — the "re-graded by judgment" the refusal prescribes. `retire-identity --code SCI` still refused: `evidence_population_match.target_population (1)`.
- **Scope today:** MOB (59 match rows), MS (1) and SCI (1) cannot be retired by any CLI path.
- **Same shape, on seeded rows:**
  - a resolved `determination_gates` row still counts as a live carrier (`resolved_at` is not read as a retirement mark);
  - so does a `CLOSED-*` gap;
  - so does a `search_executions.identity_code` row.
  `amend-gap` and `amend-search` cannot change the code on these, and no re-tag verb for gates is in the verb list.

## 4. T-054 — a writer is sent to a successor that is itself deprecated (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `_identity_carriers` excludes `superseded_by_identity` from the carriers; `dbcore.check_identity_live` (`scripts/dbcore.py`) reads one hop.
- **Shown:** `retire-identity --code VES --to-identity EPI`, then `retire-identity --code EPI --need A-STABLE` — both rc=0. Then `add-lens-link --identity VES` refuses with "Use the identity code 'EPI' instead", and EPI is deprecated.
- **Why the test missed it:** T054-03 covers "to a deprecated code" only at retirement time, never the successor being retired afterwards.

## 5. T-054 — a retired crossing is re-opened by one character (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py:9152-9161` (the clash check in `insert_population_icf_link`).
- **Claim:** "A retired crossing is never un-retired."
- **Shown:** I retired link 22 (`SCI`, `d410`, "Biomechanical + autonomic"). `add-population-icf-link` with the mechanism "Biomechanical + autonomic." (a full stop added) returned rc=0 as link 62. The engine and `derivation_handshake_integrity` read `(identity, icf)` over live rows, so the crossing is back.
- **Second defect in the same path:** re-adding the identical row is refused with "link 22 already maps SCI -> d410 by this mechanism", never saying link 22 is retired. A crossing retired by mistake can only be restored by rewording its mechanism.

## 6. T-054 — any Owner heading approves any retirement, and nothing is stored (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `_owner_approval` (`scripts/db.py:8754`) and `retire_identity`.
- **Shown:** MOVE, VES and EPI were all retired on scratch with `--approval-ref "Owner instruction 2026-11-15 (later) — at the end of each batch, sweep the changes forward and backward…"` and `--reason t`. The heading is about batch sweeps. The gate asks whether the heading begins "Owner" and is dated, not whether it concerns the code.
- **What the row keeps:** only `updated_at`. `retire_identity` never uses its `session` parameter, and the reason and approval are printed, not stored (as the task specifies).
- **Why the test cannot see it:** T-054's own tests pick `_OH54` as the first dated Owner heading in the ledger, whatever it says.
- **Ruling that does exist:** `references/project-standards.md:6015` (OD-37) covers MOVE and VES. Nothing ties the verb to it.

## 7. T-048 — the registry admits one root twice, and an admitted source as "external" (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `register_root` in `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py`.
- **Shown on scratch**, all rc=0:
  - `ROOT-A` "Steinfeld 1979 lab study" and `root-a` " steinfeld 1979 LAB study " both registered. The view `v_registry_duplicate_descriptions` then lists the pair; the writer does not read it.
  - `REF-00987`, an admitted source's ref_id, registered as an external root.
  - Pointing extractions 119, 120 and 121 at these (plus `root_type`) raised `v_value_independence.independent_root_count` for parameter 3 from 14 to 17.
- **Unread required field:** `--root-type` is `required=True`, but `v_value_independence` reads `source_value_extractions.root_type`, not the registry's. `ROOT-A` was registered `committee_assertion` and counted as `measurement_primary` through extraction 119's own column. Nothing refused the contradiction.
- **Two roots on one row:** `amend-extraction --extraction-id 46 --field root_id --value ROOT-A` on a row that already has `root_ref_id='REF-00979'` returned rc=0. `COALESCE(root_ref_id, root_id)` then ignores the root_id. `insert_extraction` does not refuse this either, so amend skips no refusal add has; neither has one.

## 8. T-027 — "edition" is counted as done for sources it cannot reach; `original_title` had the same small step available (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` (`_BIBLIO_FIELDS`, the `("edition", lambda m: m.get("edition-number"))` entry) and `/home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-15-remediation-stack/sweep-list.md:59-60`.
- **Edition:** the task's problem is "a standard's edition … A superseded edition can be cited as current". `correct-source` writes edition only from a Crossref `edition-number`.
  - `select tier, count(*), sum(coalesce(doi,'')<>'') from evidence_sources group by tier` gives tiers 4, 5 and 6 as 2, 7 and 21 rows with 0 DOIs. No standard can receive an edition.
  - The evidence command still prints `sum(edition is not null) = 0`.
  - T027-05 asserts `"edition" in db._CORRECTABLE`. That is a set-membership test and cannot go red on an edition never being written.
- **`original_title`:** the sweep-list reason is "a national standard's original title has no Crossref payload". That argument applies word for word to edition, which the same entry counts as done. Meanwhile the logged payloads do carry it: a scan of `retrieval-log/**/*.json` for a non-empty `original-title` array found 10 (Japanese and Korean titles, e.g. `retrieval-log/session_2026-09-12-b5b-scope-rulings/ac2a86db5cbeca4c.json`). One `_BIBLIO_FIELDS` entry of the same shape as edition's was available.
- **`v_evidence_authors`:** `[NULL: the deferral — evidence_source_authors has no column marking a name without an initials convention; I found no smaller correct step]`.

## 9. T-034 — lens and jurisdiction filters are ignored outside judgment and specification (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `cell_status`: `scan()`, the synthesis block, and `gates` filter on `parameter_id` only.
- **Shown:**
  - `cell-status --parameter-id 3 --identity SCI` returns judgment `[158,159,160]` (correct), but evidence `held` has 57 refs when only `REF-01033` carries an SCI figure.
  - The same call lists `open_gates: [1]`, and gate 1 is `identity_code='MOB'`.
  - `--jurisdiction US` narrows judgment to 23 and leaves evidence at 57.
  - `--jurisdiction ISO` returns no pairs at all, hence nothing owed, because `lang_jur_map` has no ISO, INT, UN, HR or UG row.
- **Unused columns:** `search_executions`, `gaps` and `determination_gates` all carry lens columns; `gaps` also has jurisdiction and language.
- **Why the test missed it:** T034-03 is titled "no other stage's list is made up" and asserts only `judgment.held`. No case exercises `--jurisdiction` or `--language` beyond the refusals.

## 10. T-027 — currency is stamped on rows it does not apply to (MEDIUM)

- **Artefact:** `amend_source`, `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py:6446-6453` and `6579-6581`.
- **Shown:**
  - `REF-00979` (tier 1, clinical) accepted `PERMANENT-FRAMEWORK`, then `SUPERSEDED-PENDING-REPLACEMENT`. `governance/tier-system.md` §4 scopes the check to T4–T6 citations.
  - `REF-01019`, a tombstone with `superseded_by_ref_id` set, accepted `VERIFIED-CURRENT`.
  - The first currency write on a row with NULL `metadata_integrity_status` set it to `CORRECTED` and ledgered "code_currency_status CORRECTED (r). Replaced text was: None". A first assertion is recorded as a metadata correction. 35 of 59 rows are NULL there today.
- **No way back:** a blank is refused, so a status once set can never be withdrawn.

## 11. T-027 — the vocabulary parse fails quietly in two directions (LOW)

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/dbcore.py:383-391`.
- **Read from the regex, not run against a reworded file:**
  - `` `([A-Z][A-Z-]+)` `` on the first line containing `` `code_currency_status` enum: `` admits any backticked upper-case token later added to that line as a legal status.
  - It silently drops a value containing a digit or underscore.
  - If the sentence is reworded or wrapped, the result is `[]` and the verb refuses everything (fail-closed, good).
- **Gate that then examines nothing:** in that case the whole T027 section prints one `skip("T027", …)`, so the gate is green with no case run.
- **Second home:** line 55 of `governance/tier-system.md` is now a prose caller that code parses, with no gate on it.

## 12. T-054 — schema and message gaps (LOW)

Schema (seeded on scratch):
- `status` is nullable. `INSERT … status NULL, superseded_by_need 'A-SIZE'` passes the new CHECK, and `check_identity_live` treats the row as live.
- A child with NULL status is not counted as a `parent_code` carrier, so its parent retires over it.
- The schema accepts a self-successor (`ZZ4 → ZZ4`); only the verb refuses it.
- `retired_at=''` with `''` for the other two columns passes the crossing CHECK. Readers (`retired_at IS NULL`) call that row retired; the writer (`if row["retired_at"]`) calls it live.
- `UPDATE identity_icf_map SET retired_at=NULL, …` succeeds. "Never un-retired" is held by the absence of a verb, not by the schema.

Messages:
- `assess_cell.py:2030-2034` and `add-identity --parent` refuse a deprecated code without naming the successor.
- `add-conflict`, `add-population-match` and `add-population-icf-link` say "Use the access need 'A-PRECISION' (--needs / a need lens)" but have no `--needs` flag.
- `amend-identity --code MOVE --display-name Movers` succeeds on a deprecated code.

## 13. T-034 — smaller defects (LOW)

- The ledger status `BLOCKED` is in none of the four evidence lists. It has 0 rows today, so this is unproven rather than clean. T034-02 hard-codes the same five statuses.
- With two lens codes, judgment accepts a figure whose codes sit on separate link rows (extraction 165 for `--identity MS --needs A-EFFORT`), while specification requires one row carrying both.
- `--identity ''` is silently unfiltered.
- The docstring and commit message say the pairs come from `v_research_scope`; the code never reads the view and restates its rule in Python.
- `open_gaps` has no subject: `select count(*) from gaps where parameter_id is not null` returns 0.
- A scoped-out pair that was searched appears in no pair list.

## 14. T-048 — smaller defects (LOW)

- `root_id` can be repointed but never cleared (a blank is refused).
- `--population-note ' '` is stored as `' '`.
- A one-character `--provenance` passes as the warrant.
- `register_root` sits between `_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS` and the comment block that documents it.

---

## Attacks that found nothing

- `[NULL: cell-status writes — 13 calls on a copy; every table's row count, the file sha256, mtime and PRAGMA data_version identical before and after]`
- `[NULL: cell-status id lists against independent SQL for parameters 3, 5, 7 and lens MOB/SCI — judgment, ledger statuses (58 = 58, no duplicates), specifications held/retired and gates all match the tables; no invented id, no double count]`
- `[NULL: migration 135 CHECK on write paths — status→deprecated without successor, successor on an active row, second successor, INSERT of a deprecated row without successor, status→active with successor left: all refused with IntegrityError]`
- `[NULL: rebuild — migrate_db.py --rebuild at 136: 161 objects, 0 sqlite_master differences, 59 tables row-identical except data_migrations.applied_at/notes]`
- `[NULL: containment of eca7ea8f's database change — only base_taxonomy_identity and identity_icf_map DDL changed; no pre-existing column's rows moved in any table; 0 rows carry a successor or a retirement]`
- `[NULL: retire-identity carriers, each seeded in isolation — conflicts.pop_a/pop_b, connection_targets, open determination_gates, live extraction_lens_links, live identity_icf_map, identity_medical_map, search_executions, gaps, evidence_population_match.target_population, parent_code of an active child: all refused and named. Retired specification, retired lens link and retired crossing do not block, as the task defines live]`
- `[NULL: identity codes in columns with no FK — scanned every text column of every table for exact codes; only evidence_population_match.target_population (61 of 61) holds them. term_aliases.alias holds 14 code-shaped strings, not examined further]`
- `[NULL: deprecated code refused, successor named — add-population-match, add-population-icf-link, raise-determination-gate, add-lens-link, add-gap, add-connection, log-search, add-conflict --pop-a and --pop-b]`
- `[NULL: readers of identity_icf_map — git grep over scripts, skills, .claude; sqlite_master (one index, no view or trigger). assess_cell.py:620 and derivation_handshake_integrity.py:113 both filter retired_at IS NULL; no skill reads the table]`
- `[NULL: register-root — whitespace-only provenance and description refused; unknown type refused by the CHECK; duplicate id refused; created_at and created_by_session written; a .md session stored as the stem]`
